title: PIL does not pack 2-bit palette images correctly

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Any unexpected behavior, until confirmed feature.

body:
```Python
from PIL import Image

rgb = '\x00' * 2 + '\x01' * 2 + '\x02' * 2
img = Image.frombytes('P', (6, 1), rgb)
img.putpalette('\xFF\x00\x00' '\x00\xFF\x00' '\x00\x00\xFF') # RGB
img.save('file.png')
```
Expected is an image with 6 pixels: `RRGGBB`. Instead it makes image `RRGGBR`.

The first clue is in the raw (uncompressed) `IDAT` bytes written: `0x00 0x05 0x80`.

Now the first byte is the filter byte, and the bit representation of the other two bytes is as follows.
```
0x05: 00 00 01 01
0x80: 10 00 00 00
```
Whereas it should be.
```
0x05: 00 00 01 01
0xA0: 10 10 00 00
```
So `10` is `00`, hence `R` instead of `B`.

The packing is handled by function `packP2`.

```c
static void
packP2(UINT8* out, const UINT8* in, int pixels)
{
    while (pixels >= 4) {
	*out++ = (in[0] << 6) |
		 ((in[1] & 3) << 4) |
		 ((in[2] & 3) << 2) |
		 (in[3] & 3);
	in += 4; pixels -= 4;
    }

    switch (pixels) {
    case 3:
	out[0] = (in[0] << 6) |
		 ((in[1] & 3) << 4) |
		 ((in[2] & 3) << 2);
	break;
    case 2:
	out[0] = (in[0] << 6) |
		 ((in[1] & 3) << 4);
    case 1:
	out[0] = (in[0] << 6);
    }
}
```
Which has an obvious bug making it pack only the first of two remaining pixels.
```Diff
index 8a0fcc0..af32392 100644
--- a/libImaging/Pack.c
+++ b/libImaging/Pack.c
@@ -194,6 +194,7 @@ packP2(UINT8* out, const UINT8* in, int pixels)
     case 2:
        out[0] = (in[0] << 6) |
                 ((in[1] & 3) << 4);
+    break;
     case 1:
        out[0] = (in[0] << 6);
     }
```
